skill.name: docs-validator
skill.description: Documentation quality validator for Logseq Template Graph. Checks documentation completeness, accuracy, formatting, links, and consistency. Activates when asked to "validate docs", "check documentation", "audit docs quality", "find broken links", or similar requests. Provides actionable feedback and specific fixes for documentation issues.
skill.summary: Audit Logseq Template Graph documentation for coverage, accuracy, formatting, links, and consistency.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: All 42 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, safe read-only shell examples, placeholder URLs, a relative link, and checklist prose. Semantic review identified two medium risks: unrestricted external URL testing and optional execution of documentation examples without explicit isolation controls.

remediation.issue: External link validation can access repository-controlled destinations, including private or local addresses.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only HTTP and HTTPS, block loopback and private networks, set strict timeouts, and require confirmation before contacting untrusted domains.

remediation.issue: Testing commands or code examples can execute content controlled by the repository.
remediation.suggestion: Default to syntax-only checks. Require explicit approval and an isolated sandbox before executing any documented command or code example.

content.value_statement: Incomplete documentation causes broken links, missing guides, and inconsistent project information. This skill audits Logseq Template Graph documentation and provides prioritized fixes.
actual_capabilities: Inventories Markdown documentation and module README files across project directories.
Checks documentation completeness for modules, guides, APIs, features, and examples.
Finds broken internal and external links and suggests specific replacements.
Reviews Markdown headings, lists, tables, code fences, and document structure.
Compares terminology, feature status, versions, and project facts for consistency.
Produces prioritized reports with scores, coverage metrics, issue locations, and suggested fixes.
limitations: The workflow assumes Logseq Template Graph directories and requires adaptation for other repositories.
External URL checks require network access and can fail during temporary remote outages.
Accuracy checks require project source context and cannot independently prove every documentation claim.
Shell examples are illustrative and may require adjustment for different platforms.

use_cases.title: Maintain Documentation Quality
use_cases.description: Find missing pages, formatting problems, inconsistent terms, and broken references before documentation changes are merged.

use_cases.title: Measure Module Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare source modules with README files and prioritize undocumented features or examples.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Documentation
use_cases.description: Audit links, versions, commands, feature status, and user guides before a release.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Quick Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the project documentation. Report coverage, missing module README files, and the three most important issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for an immediate quality summary

prompt_templates.title: Check All Links
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate internal and external documentation links. List each broken link, its location, impact, and a suggested replacement.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Coverage and Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit module coverage, feature documentation, terminology, Markdown formatting, examples, and version references. Prioritize findings by impact.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Release Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full pre-release documentation audit. Verify coverage, links, formatting, examples, accuracy, and consistency. Produce prioritized fixes and measurable scores.

output: Top issue: the misc module has no README file.

output_examples.input: Check the documentation for broken links.
output: Broken external link found in the installation guide.
Dead internal setup link found in the documentation index.
Each issue includes its location, priority, and suggested destination.

output_examples.output: The report summarizes coverage, accuracy, formatting, links, and consistency, then lists prioritized fixes with estimated impact.

best_practices: Run focused checks during development and a full audit before each release.
Review proposed fixes against source behavior before changing technical documentation.
Track coverage and issue counts over time to identify recurring gaps.
anti_patterns: Do not execute documentation commands without reviewing their safety and obtaining approval.
Do not treat temporary network failures as proof that an external link is permanently broken.
Do not apply placeholder fixes without confirming the correct target, terminology, or version.

faq.question: What documentation does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Markdown files, module README files, user guides, technical documentation, feature coverage, links, and examples.

faq.question: Can it find broken links?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks relative references and can test external URLs when network access is available.

faq.question: Does it edit documentation automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow focuses on reports and suggested fixes. Apply changes only after reviewing each recommendation.

faq.question: Can it validate another repository?
faq.answer: Yes, after adapting the project-specific directories, module counts, terminology, and coverage expectations.

faq.question: Does it execute code examples?
faq.answer: It may propose testing examples. Use syntax checks first, then require approval and isolation before execution.

faq.question: What report formats are supported?
faq.answer: The skill describes console summaries, Markdown reports, machine-readable exports, and issue lists suitable for GitHub tracking.
